chunks: We performed hajj with Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) in the year in which his son Mūsā (عليه السلام) was born. When we encamped at al-Abwāʾ, he set out lunch for us, and whenever he placed food for his companions, he would make it more abundant and better.

He said: While we were eating, a messenger from Ḥamīdah came to him and said: Ḥamīdah says, “I feel the change in myself, and I have found what I used to find when my delivery approached, and you instructed me not to precede you regarding this son of yours.” So Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) arose and went with the messenger.

When he returned, his companions said to him: May Allah gladden you, and may we be your ransom; what happened with Ḥamīdah? He said: Allah kept her safe and has granted me a غلام, and he is the best of those whom Allah created among His creation. Ḥamīdah informed me about him with a matter she thought I did not know, while I knew it better than she did.

I said: May I be your ransom, what was it that Ḥamīdah informed you about him? He said: She mentioned that when he came forth from her womb, he came forth placing his hands upon the earth and raising his head toward the sky. So I informed her that this is the sign of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and the sign of the waṣī after him.

I said: May I be your ransom, how is this among the signs of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and the sign of the waṣī after him? He said to me: When it was the night on which my grandfather was conceived, a visitor came to my father’s grandfather with a cup containing a drink thinner than water, softer than butter, sweeter than honey, colder than ice, and whiter than milk. He gave it to him to drink and instructed him to have intercourse. So he rose, had intercourse, and my grandfather was conceived.

Then when it was the night on which my father was conceived, a visitor came to my grandfather and gave him to drink just as he had given my father’s grandfather to drink, and instructed him with the like of what he had instructed him. So he rose, had intercourse, and my father was conceived. And when it was the night on which I was conceived, a visitor came to my father and gave him to drink what he had given them, and instructed him with what he had instructed them. So he rose, had intercourse, and I was conceived.

And when it was the night on which my son was conceived, a visitor came to me just as he had come to them, and he did with me as he had done with them. So I rose by the knowledge of Allah, and I was joyful in what Allah would grant me. Then I had intercourse and this newborn son of mine was conceived. So here he is before you; by Allah, he is your master after me.

The nطفة of the Imam is as I have informed you. When the nطفة settles in the womb for four months and the spirit is formed within it, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sends an angel called Ḥayawān, and he writes upon his right upper arm:
And the word of your Lord has been completed in truth and justice; there is no changer of His words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.

When he falls forth from his mother’s womb, he comes forth placing his hands upon the earth and raising his head toward the sky. As for his placing his hands upon the earth, it is because he receives every knowledge belonging to Allah that He has sent down from the heaven to the earth. And as for his raising his head toward the sky, a caller calls him from the midst of the Throne, from the Lord of Might, from the highest horizon, by his name and the name of his father.

He says: O so-and-so son of so-and-so, be firm and you shall be made firm, for I created you for a tremendous matter. You are My chosen one from among My creation, the place of My secret, the repository of My knowledge, My trustee over My revelation, and My khalīfah in My earth. For you and for whoever holds your wilayah, I have made My mercy obligatory, granted My gardens, and permitted My nearness. Then, by My might and My majesty, I shall surely make whoever opposes you enter the severest of My punishment, even if I grant him abundance in My world from the vastness of My provision.
Then when the voice of the caller comes to an end, he answers him while placing his hands and raising his head toward the sky, saying:
Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels and those possessed of knowledge, upholding justice; there is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise.

He said: When he says that, Allah gives him the first knowledge and the last knowledge, and he becomes entitled to the visitation of the Spirit on Laylat al-Qadr. I said: May I be your ransom, is the Spirit not Jibrāʾīl? He said: The Spirit is greater than Jibrāʾīl. Jibrāʾīl is among the angels, while the Spirit is a creation greater than the angels. Does Allah, Blessed and Exalted, not say:
The angels and the Spirit descend.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from al-Mukhtār ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān, from his father, from Abū Baṣīr: similarly to it.

key_terms.أَمَارَةُ: a distinguishing sign or mark indicating a divinely recognized status
key_terms.الرُّوحُ: a created being greater than the angels, distinct from Jibrāʾīl in this narration
key_terms.الْعِلْمَ: divinely granted knowledge bestowed upon the Imam
key_terms.الْوَصِيِّ: the designated successor after the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)
key_terms.خَلِيفَتِي: My deputy or vicegerent in the earth
key_terms.صَاحِبُكُمْ: your master or authority after me
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ: the Night of Decree, during which the Spirit visits
key_terms.نُطْفَةَ: the seed or drop from which conception begins

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the birth signs and divinely granted knowledge of the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration describes the birth of Imām Mūsā (عليه السلام) and presents distinctive signs associated with the birth and conception of the Imams. It explains, in theological terms, their divinely marked origin, their reception of special knowledge, and their connection to the Spirit on Laylat al-Qadr. The report also cites Qur'anic passages to frame the Imam’s station, knowledge, and divine appointment.
